issues.issue: The Schedule states "Additional Ratings Not Applicable" while assigning a 150% substandard Risk Classification, which cannot be squared with the acceptance-form amendment "Base policy is rated" (c168) and with the Monthly Deduction component (d) for Additional Ratings in Section 9.

The notice requires "the Net Policy Value, less Policy Debt" to cover deductions, but Section 3 already defines Net Policy Value as Policy Value less Policy Debt (c026), so debt is deducted twice against the Section 11 lapse test.
The table fixes the Cost of Insurance Charge only by reference to Section 9 and the Section 2 maximum rates, so its meaning depends entirely on the contested rate-setting language in c070/c072.
The Schedule shows a Rider Charge of "None" for the Living Benefit Rider, while the rider itself authorises an Administrative Charge on payment (c155).
The $1,000,000 Maximum Annual Premium sits against Section 4's promise that "in no event will we refuse to accept any premium necessary to prevent the policy from terminating" (c041).

This footnote asserts an unqualified "right to change ... the amount of cost of insurance deducted under the policy," which cannot be squared with Section 9's limits on re-determining COI rates (c072) and its enumerated rate factors (c070).
"We have the right to change ... the amount of cost of insurance" states no standard or limit, leaving open whether the right is unfettered or governed by Section 9.
The 1980 CSO basis fixes only the Section 2 guaranteed maximum rates, leaving its relationship to the current-rate provision in Section 9 (c070) open to argument.

The unisex Monthly Factor is stated as "4.0032737" where the corresponding factor in the same table is 1.0032737, a transcription error that would materially change every Net Amount at Risk calculation.
"Age 100 Anniversary" (Policy Anniversary nearest the 100th birthday) and "Maturity Date" (Attained Age 100, c023) are separately defined and need not fall on the same date.

Defining Attained Age as "the Age plus the number of whole years that have elapsed since the Policy Date" double-counts, because "Age" is itself defined as the current age at the nearest birthday rather than the age at issue.
"Any day that we are open for business" defines the term by reference to the insurer's own unstated practice, giving no ascertainable boundary.
The catch-all "any other proof acceptable to us" follows two specific items and gives the insurer sole say over what suffices, leaving the reach of the definition uncertain.

The definition requires a "written form signed by you, satisfactory to us" but then adds "or such other medium electronic or otherwise that we may from time to time make available," so whether signature and satisfaction are always required is unclear.

The Maturity Date is defined as the date the Insured reaches Attained Age 100, yet Section 8 (c059-c063) provides for continuing coverage, interest crediting and default on or after that date, so nothing actually "matures."
The Schedule notice (c005) speaks of "the Net Policy Value, less Policy Debt," which duplicates the subtraction built into this definition.
The sentence is ungrammatical ("that you intend to be pay on a regular modal basis") and ends without punctuation, though the intended sense is recoverable.
The opening formula credits Net Premium "less an amount not to exceed one month of Monthly Deductions," which fixes only a ceiling and leaves the actual initial deduction indeterminate.
The definition trails off after "less any unpaid issue charges," leaving the sentence incomplete on the face of the instrument.
"We" refers only to the Company here, while the Living Benefit Rider defines "We" as Phoenix "or its subsidiaries" (c145).

"We reserve the right to make any reasonable adjustments to the terms or conditions of this policy ... to the extent we deem it necessary" combines an objective standard ("reasonable") with a subjective one ("we deem") and sets no boundary on what may be adjusted.
The reserved unilateral power to adjust terms sits against Section 22 (c134), which requires any change in the provisions of the policy to be in writing signed and countersigned by officers.

"In no event, however, will we refuse to accept any premium necessary to prevent the policy from terminating" contradicts Section 4's reserved right to refuse premiums failing the elected test (c040) and Section 10's directive not to process such payments (c081).

The Cash Value Accumulation Test terms, including a retroactive right to modify Death Benefit Percentages, are inoperative on their face because Section 1 records the Guideline Premium Test as the elected, unchangeable test.

A pro-rata Surrender Charge is imposed on any face reduction here, whereas Section 6 says a face reduction on a Death Benefit Option change carries "no change to the surrender charge schedule" (c054).

The rule that no Death Proceeds are paid once a surrender request is received depends on Section 15's statement that after receipt "no insurance will be in force" (c111), and neither addresses a request received but not yet processed.
